utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. We're pleased to inform the Chamber that the witness is feeling better. I just want to let the Chamber know that he has, I think, some back issues, and so perhaps if there is any discomfort, I'm sure he will indicate that to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And Ms. Mahindaratne will be leading the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will call in the witness then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I ask you to take the card that is to be offered to you, and if you would then make the affirmation. If you would stand for that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Examined by Ms. Mahindaratne:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Negodic.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, could you please state your full name and age.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Ivan Negodic, born on the 8th of September, 1947, in Herceg Novi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you also referred to by a nickname, and if so, could you please state that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Braco.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where do you live?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: In Dubrovnik, Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since when have you lived in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: I'm a pensioner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your occupation prior to retirement?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: I was head of the technical service of a big hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your ethnic origin?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: A Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, could you please briefly describe your academic and professional background.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: [In English] Electrotechnical school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you hear me, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness said in English, "electrotechnical school." Interpreter's note.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard you. Are you asking me about my private life now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I'm not. Have you had any military training or been in military service?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did my military service at the reserve officer school in Zadar, and after that I was transferred to Pozaverac in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please give a detailed description of the military training that you obtained and in particular, reference to the weapons training that you had?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: I completed the military school in Zadar. After that, I was trained in Pozaverac, too, so it was a total of 19 months. After that, several courses in Zadar, Slavonska Posega [phoen], Zagreb, altogether approximately about a thousand days on the reserve force of Yugoslavia. That will do for the time being.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of your military training, did you have training in specific weapon systems, such as training in mortars or artillery?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes. At the school there was some theory and some practice. Howitzers, 122 millimetres, 155, the cannon howitzer 203, 120-millimetre howitzers. After that I was transferred to Pozarevac for the second part of my military service, and that's where I used 120-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give us some understanding about the ranks you held within the JNA and thereafter, if you served in any other force. First if you start off with the JNA, the particular ranks you held.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Until Yugoslavia fell apart, I held the rank of captain first class. After that, with the same rank, I was in the Croatian army. In the beginning of 1992, I got the rank of major.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the time of retirement from the military, you held the rank of major. Is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, but that was not the case in civilian life. It didn't really matter in civilian life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course. Prior to the conflict in Dubrovnik, what -- what was your occupation? You stated earlier on that you were the head of -- head technician at a hotel. Was that the same post that you held prior to the conflict in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until when did you work in this capacity?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Until the month of July 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you be able to tell the Trial Chamber as to what happened in the month of July, end of -- did you say end? Month of July 1991.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: We, in the area of Dubrovnik, knew that in the area of Dubrovnik [as interpreted] there was a troublesome situation already. When we look at --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is a transcript issue. I believe it was said in the area of Vukovar there was a troublesome situation, and I think it came out as Dubrovnik. If it's possible -- I apologise for interrupting my colleague, but I believe it was an error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps you would clarify that matter, if you would, with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, could you repeat your answer again. I'm sorry for inconveniencing you.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Since we learned about things through the media that in the area of Vukovar there was a troublesome situation, and the Serbs in Dubrovnik, just near the territory of the town of Dubrovnik, caused a similar situation and therefore we had to prepare ourselves, at least in some way, for a possible attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I take your response to mean that after -- in July 1991 or since then you were involved in preparation against -- against a potential attack? Is that how I should understand your response to me?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, but working on paper problems, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I use the term administrative aspects is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: This administrative phrasing is a better solution, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And against what were you preparing to defend? What was the objective behind these preparations? Could you be a lit bit more -- could you perhaps elaborate a little bit more clearly? If I could make it -- if I could say was there a particular threat, and if so, what was the threat?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: It was a public secret, so to speak. We do not have ten enemies, only one who wanted our territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whom did you perceive as the enemy? Could you give it a name?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: The command, military and civilian, from the territory of Serbia and Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say military, what military are you talking about? What was this particular military force known as? What was the name? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: The JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: The Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us as to what other steps did you take towards organisation of the defence against this army. That is, what role did you play in the organisation of the defence?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: I was chief of artillery, and I was supposed to look through the administration of the Territorial Defence headquarters so that I would take care of my units on paper, so to speak, although I didn't really have any, especially not with weapons.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please be asked to speak up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you speak up a little.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving forward from the phase -- administrative phrase, could you be a little bit more specific with regard to your role in the organisation of the Dubrovnik defence? And I'm asking you to move forward from the administrative phase into the active phase.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: As for the active phase, again it is directly linked to the administrative phase. All lower-ranking officers and non-commissioned officers who completed military courses or schools in the former JNA were supposed to be made available to me as persons who were closest to me, and they were supposed to train the rest of the men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So were you -- in effect, what you're saying is that you were involved in the organisation of recruitment with regard to perhaps the artillery division. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, indirectly, because this is the basic task of the Territorial Defence staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the aspects of recruitment, were you also involved in securing weapons and heavy weapons, in fact - I'm specifically referring to heavy weapons - for the Dubrovnik defence force. When I say "securing," I'm not talking about physical securing, organisation of the securing aspect.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about training? Were you involved in any -- in a -- any aspect of the organisation of the training of personnel in the artillery divisions? If I may rephrase, artillery sector.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, initially.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the territory that you -- your force was attempting to defend against the JNA? Could you identify it by name? You don't have to go into every areas and municipalities. I'm asking you what was the particular territory, the broader area?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: If we look towards the border with Montenegro, then it is the territory of Konavle. If we look towards Bosnia-Herzegovina, then it is the territory of the coast, Rijeka Dubrovacka, and Mokosica. Brgat is in the middle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, the territory of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the wider area of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you said that you were the head of the artillery sector for -- I'm sorry, the term you used was chief of artillery sector of the Dubrovnik defence force. Were you at any stage formally appointed to this position?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. That's the way it was supposed to be, and that is the military system, that I should have my appointment confirmed from Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Could I have the assistance of Madam Usher to show a document to the witness. I think it's on Sanction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this document which has just been placed before you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: This is the usual kind of proposal for appointment. However, this is just a confirmation of the proposal that had been approved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this document is dated 1 November 1991. However, in this document, the -- you can clearly see by the sixth and the seventh lines that you are being confirmed in the post of chief of sectors artillery and that you clearly held that position from prior to 1 November 1991. Isn't that the case, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since when did you hold this position? You said you were involved in organisation of the artillery sector at the beginning of the formation of the force. Was it the case that you held this position from the beginning of the force itself, from prior to 1st of October, 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was sent on the 28th of August. Of course the year is 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you be more specific? You said you were sent on the 28th of August. Was there a formal formation of the Dubrovnik defence force by 28th of August, 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: The 28th of August was not when the town's defence was established. It was just under the process of being established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When would you say was the town's defence was formally established. Could you be able to give an approximate time or date, perhaps, or a month -- or the month?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: If you mean when the town's defence was established, then I can say that the town's defence was not fully established even by the new year of 1992. However, what was established was the formation of the units as we received weapons and artillery pieces and ammunition. So that's how we were able to set up the units, in line with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what time frame would you give for that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: That took place, roughly speaking, in October, as far as the artillery was concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in that context would it be correct to say that you were -- you were chief of artillery sector of the Dubrovnik defence since October 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Not with respect to the men. I -- I started preparations with the men from the 28th of August with reconnaissance work towards the border with Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I move to tender this document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is P158.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you briefly describe the composition of the Dubrovnik defence force. And when I say composition of the force, I'm referring to the personnel. You don't have to give me the exact numbers, but as to who consisted of the force? Were they reservists, professional soldiers, ordinary people? Just some idea.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: For the lower units, they were people who had gone to the reserve officers school and graduated from that, non-commissioned officers and lower-ranking officers, and then there were people who lived in Dubrovnik, the inhabitants of Dubrovnik as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any professional soldiers in the force?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Not in the artillery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the entire force? I'm not specifically referring only to artillery.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes. Four men in the headquarters and command for the staff's -- for the town's defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As such, how would you describe the level of training of the personnel attached to the artillery sector, and that is your sector? And just to make it convenient for you, I will give you a point of reference as 6th December 1991. As at 6 December 1991, what was the level of training?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer, please?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: It was quite solid or average. The artillery pieces were handled by people who were sufficiently trained. They had been to the reserve officers school, or they were uncommissioned officers or lower-ranking officers. The other men were from the rank and file, that is to say, ordinary citizens who didn't have the necessary knowledge but who didn't actually need any professional training for the kind of work they did. All they needed was a short training course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have these ordinary people, as you put it, attached to the artillery sector of the force, or did you have reservists attached to the artillery sector, and if both, could you give some idea as to what the percentages were?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: In the former Yugoslavia, every man who had done his military service pursuant to the law and the reigning system was a reserve officer or soldier of the former Yugoslavia. Now, in that sense, everyone who had completed the army was automatically a reservist, made up the reserve composition in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So are you saying that all the personnel attached to the artillery sector were reservists with some military background?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the personnel who were given the responsibility of manning the weapons in your sector all trained in those particular weaponry that they had to handle? And if so, could you give some idea as to their level of training, was it acceptable in that sense?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Otherwise, they wouldn't have been able to perform the tasks and assignments they were given.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if there were members of the ZNG, the Croatian National Guard, within the Dubrovnik defence force? And I'm not particularly referring to your artillery sector but the entire force.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Not in the artillery. In the Dubrovnik defence, yes, in several units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In reference to weapons, how and from where were weapons obtained for the force?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, from the Metkovic-Ploce direction, and the Peljesac Peninsula, Elafiti Dubrovnik, which means Mljet, Sipan, Lopud, those islands, Kolocep, Lapad as part of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were weapons obtained from any islands around the -- around Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were these islands? Can you name them?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Korcula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other islands apart from Korcula?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were others too. We got the 85-millimetre cannons, they arrived afterwards. If you mean for 1991 or in 1991, then there were just two Zis's and mortars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By October 1991, can you give the Trial Chamber some idea as to what the presence of the JNA in the area was like. Was there a concentrated, strong presence of JNA units in the area? And I'm referring to the time period perhaps 1st October 1991.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: The JNA, at the beginning of October, broke through the border crossing towards Konavle, and the forces that were in Konavle withdrew towards the Dubrovacka-Zupa area, and after that to the Brgat area, and after that again to the narrow area of the town and the fort of Srdj above the town. On the 24th of October, a naval landing took place in the Dubrovacka-Zupa area and Kupari area, and this attack was launched from the sea. It was assisted by the paramilitaries from the northern section, Trebinje, Nevesinje, Niksic, Bijelo Polje area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that by 24th October there was a land and sea blockade of Dubrovnik by the JNA forces?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes. Between the 24th and 25th, Dubrovnik was in a blockade, because from the sea there was no more access. They didn't have access to anybody any more because they were prevented in doing so by the naval vessels belonging to the Yugoslav navy. They prevented any comings or goings and controlled the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the context of the blockade -- I rephrase that term. I'm sorry, Your Honours. You said you obtained your weapons from the islands. From where did you -- as well as some other areas. From where did you obtain your ammunition?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: We obtained our ammunition from the Metkovic-Ploce direction and the peninsula Peljesac, and the only transportation towards Dubrovnik was with motor boats, speed boats, and ammunition would be brought in in the speed boats, and they would go island hopping during the night and unload in Lapad on the big beach there at Lapad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was going to be my next question. In the context of the blockade, the land and the sea blockade, how did your forces succeed in getting supplies of weapons and ammunition without being detected by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: The movement of vessels was monitored. The speed boats had high-power motors, and between the islands they didn't need much time and to wait for the next -- for the following night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So supplies for all this made during night-time to avoid detection by JNA [sic]?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of any incidents where your supply boats were in fact defected by the JNA, and if so, what consequences ensued?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: There were small skirmishes, but it was like the battle between David and Goliath.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you said David and Goliath, could you give some indication as to whom -- who -- which force was which -- who? Whom are you referring to as David, and whom are you referring to as Goliath?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: David was the Croatian man in the speedboat, but he didn't have a sling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, do you know the name of the -- the forces which were deployed around Dubrovnik, the particular group was known by a particular name, or did you refer to them as the JNA? Can you identify them by a particular name?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: I would say that the majority was the JNA assisted by the paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not my question. Did you know as to whether these troops belonged to a particular group or a particular corps or a particular unit? Could you identify? Or perhaps one particular formation?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as I'm concerned, there was no time to come by that kind of information. It was enough to address the artillery problems as an artilleryman, but it was the naval military district of Boka that was responsible, and in all the orders and any requests that were made, the signature was that of Sofronije Jeremic, which means that the JNA was behind all the moves that were made in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, have you -- are you familiar or are you heard of the 2nd Operational Group of the JNA? If you are not, just say no. If you --

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't actually tell you anything much about that. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We will leave it at that. As at 6 December 1991, what was the strength of your artillery and mortar sector in terms of personnel? Just an approximate number will do.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Approximately 80 or 90.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what weapons did you have in your sector as at 6 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Two Zis 76-millimetre guns or cannons, a Maljutka type weapon, seven 82-millimetre mortars [Realtime transcript read in error "military"], three 120-millimetre mortars, a single barrel rocket launcher, 128 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is a correction to be made on the transcript. It's gone down as "82 military mortars," but it's millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the heavy weapons that you just described as being in your sector, did the Dubrovnik defence force also have infantry weapons?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be able to give the Trial Chamber an indication as to what type of infantry weapons were available? And I'm not asking for exact quantities or the exact types, but just a general idea will do.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: If you think about -- are thinking about the infantry, to the best of my knowledge, and my knowledge is not full in that area, they had rifles, light machine-guns, and at the access roads going into town from three directions hand -- hand-held rocket launchers and an APC as anti-armour equipment.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: As anti-armour equipment. Interpreter's correction. Not APC as anti-armour equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your force have anti-aircraft weapons?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Well, that didn't come under my competence, but as far as I know, they had a three-barrel weapon, a single barrel or double barrel of the 2M type, Strela 2M and Igla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us an idea as to what --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The transcript does not reflect exactly what the witness said. So would my learned colleague ask her last question, page 16, line 16, because it isn't quite clear if we read the transcript, whereas I think the witness said this, as far as I'm concerned, quite clearly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, could you please repeat your response with regard to my question, especially in relation to the last few items you described, that is, after a single barrel or double barrel of the 2M type, and then you went on to say Strela something. Could you repeat what you just said.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, but as I say this did not come under my competence, I think and I can claim that as far as the three-barrelled weapon exists, there was a three-barrelled weapon as an anti-aircraft weapon, and then there was a single barrel or double barrel weapon as well, another anti-aircraft device was the Strela 2M. There was one piece, and it was called the -- and another piece called the Igla or pin, and there was one piece of the Igla type.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give the Trial Chamber some idea as to what the level of your weapons were in terms of -- did you have an adequate supply of weapons to meet the tasks at hand?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: We didn't have enough weapons or ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you didn't have enough weapons or ammunition, I take it your supply of ammunition was also limited?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the limited ammunition available to you, what steps did you have in place to ensure that there was no wastage in meeting your fire missions?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: This could be regulated in part through the orders which were issued. However, on the 6th of December, things escaped control somewhat, because the attacks were no longer artillery attacks but were combined attacks. Artillery weapons used and tanks and infantry weapons. So that meant that we had to use more ammunition than we had envisaged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when you said the attacks were no longer artillery attacks but were combined attacks, were you referring to attacks by the JNA or are you referring to your forces using -- your forces responding? To whom -- which forces did you refer to when you say attacks, by whom?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: I meant the attacks on the part of the JNA and the paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the details you just gave in terms of numbers and the weapons and the strength of your artillery sector was as at 6th of December since that was the point of reference I gave you. Would you say that by this stage the strength of the Dubrovnik defence force had improved in terms of personnel and weapons from the initial stages of its formation in late September or October? Just a brief response, yes or no, would suffice.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the head of the Dubrovnik defence?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: General Nojko Marinovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was his predecessor or did he have a predecessor?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: At the beginning, it was Major Zeljko Pavlovic, Chief of Staff of the TO. And the first commander of the defence for Dubrovnik municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the Dubrovnik defence headquarters located?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: In August, it was in the premises of the headquarters of the Territorial Defence, and then in the Lapad area.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the name of the hotel, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you please repeat the name of the hotel you just stated.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was your command post located?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: My command post was located in the Zagreb hotel as well when there was no combat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your personnel have a particular uniform or insignia to identify themselves?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: No. There was no need because the territory was a small one, and we didn't have any way of being sent in uniforms either. I was alone. I only -- only I had the olive green uniform worn by the soldiers in the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As at 6 December were there uniforms or any form of insignia to identify members of your force?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, how would you assess the strength of the Dubrovnik defence force in comparison to the JNA units deployed in Dubrovnik in terms of infantry and heavy weaponry, and I'm referring to the entire period of the conflict from perhaps 1st of October, 1991, to, let us say, 31st December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: If we look at the general balance of power, in terms of artillery it is a ratio of one to a hundred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of infantry?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: We only had infantry units established in the zone of defence operations. However, the JNA and the paramilitaries were deployed for attack. In that sense, military logic itself makes it incumbent to have three times more people involved in the attack than those involved in the defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. So would you give some ratio? Would you be able to? Or if not, that's all right.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: I think that approximately the ratio was 1 to 50. If we are referring to military forces that are available in Dubrovnik vis-a-vis the JNA forces and the paramilitary forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you take the -- look -- look at the situation in its entire context, that is with the supply of -- limited supply of ammunition available to your forces and the limited supply of weaponry and the numbers of infantry, how would you access the entire situation?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Well, since you've mentioned ammunition, we can no longer speak about these small ratios. In my estimate, it was 1 to 1.000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, could you please state as to approximately when the first JNA attacks against Dubrovnik took place? You don't have to give the exact date or time but approximate time period.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: If you mean when the shells fell in the area of town, in the narrower sense of the word, that was already on the 24th and 23rd of October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking about a specific target or the town. I'm asking about when -- as to when the first JNA attacks and operations against Dubrovnik take place. When did the JNA attack for the first time? The initial attacks against Dubrovnik, that's what I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: The initial attacks against the town of Dubrovnik were artillery attacks on the wider area of town. The wider nucleus of town. I'm referring to the Old Town and Lapad, Gruz, and Ploce, that is to say, without any specific targets. The 23rd of October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the first infantry attacks or -- when I'm talking about attacks, I'm not necessarily talking about attacks by heavy weaponry. Were there any form of attacks, and I'm not talking particularly about operations, just at least sporadic individual attacks prior to 23rd October, 1991. Are you saying that no shots were fired before that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: From our side?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no, from the JNA.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: From the JNA side?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: You mean -- you mean personal weapons. There were just small skirmishes at the fort of Srdj, fire coming from Zarkovica aiming at Srdj. The Yugoslav People's Army, at that time, only shelled or fired at the territory irrespective of particular targets or objectives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask this question this way: When did the hostilities in the region truly -- when did it start? Approximately.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: You mean hostilities in the area of town or the broader area of the district or municipality?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Broader area.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: In the broader area, already in the month of September 1991, mortar shells were fired every day at the village of Bani, which is in the immediate vicinity of the border crossing with Montenegro. That's on the one side. On the other side, the village of Dubravka from which there is a road leading to Trebinje and further on. It's the road leading to Bosnia-Herzegovina. But that is already the month of September. We can say that these are concrete problems that Serbia and Montenegro created.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this stage I intend to have a map marked, but considering that it's only five minutes more for the break, I wonder whether -- oh, I beg your pardon. I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, you've joined me. I'm glad somebody else gets things wrong. Before you start on that, did you want to tender the document you showed the witness much earlier?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I did, Your Honour. I did move it in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Oh. Well, I've made two mistakes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May I have the assistance of the usher to show a map to the witness, the map bearing ERN number 0334-0719. Your Honours, we have already distributed copies of this map, but in the course of this testimony the witness will be making some markings on this map, and we will provide copies of the marked map also in due course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, do you recognise this map?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it a working map of the headquarters of the Dubrovnik defence?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's a working map with artillery positions marked on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it a combat deployment map showing Croat positions as well as the JNA positions?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please take us through this map, and for -- in the interests of clarity and coherence, let us go through the map position by position. If I could have the assistance of the usher to move the map to bring the western side of the map into view. Thank you. And first and foremost, Mr. Negodic, what would you say is the scale of this map?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the territory and the area that is depicted in this map? And you don't have to go into each and every area or municipality, just in general terms. Is this a map of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Rijeka Dubrovacka can be also be seen, with Mokosica, which is part of the Dubrovnik municipality. That's the northern part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just please place your pointer and indicate as to which area is Mokosica and which area is Rijeka Dubrovacka. Pardon my pronunciation.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What are you indicating right now? Could you just state for the record what you are indicating right now.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: I am indicating Rijeka Dubrovacka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is the -- the waterway that you just indicated; is that right? It's a territory beyond the waterway, beyond the --

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Of course. Now I am going to show the area of Old Mokosica and New Mokosica because there are two distinct parts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the Old Mokosica you have just indicated?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: No. Old and New Mokosica are adjoining, because if we look at it from the point of view of construction, it appears as one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just pull up the map and indicate Old Town, Stari Grad of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we'll go through the positions, the artillery and mortar positions, your positions. If you could just pull up the map, push the map so that the western end of the map shows -- comes on the ELMO. If you could pull it towards your -- that's right. Thank you. Could you place your pointer on the -- the western most position, military position, on this map that is on the coastal line on the west.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm referring to the one above. Yes. That's correct. Can you identify that location?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: This is the Maljutka position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I asked for the location. What is that location known as?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: The location is the President Hotel, near the sea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is that area called?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Lapad. The Hotel President by the sea. That's where the position is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the weapon that was positioned there, weapon or weapons? Could you indicate the type and the numbers.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Maljutka, one piece.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that particular symbol which looks like an aircraft, is that the symbol which indicates a Maljutka position?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that position deployed as at 6 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it active, as in did that Maljutka fire on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: The concentration of the attack of the Yugoslav army [as interpreted] was such that they had to withdraw into the President Hotel because no shelter had been made.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honours, the position that the witness just testified is the position indicated between -- on the western side, on the coast, between the words --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You were speaking?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I thought my learned friend --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, but if you could just finish your question and then we'll deal with what concerns --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: The position indicated between the words Rt Baterija and Rt -- I'm sorry, my pronunciation is bad. Mr. Negodic, could you pronounce it so that it goes down on record.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes. So let us take the middle between the cape. That is where the battery is, and the cap [sic] Gnjiliste.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. My request to you is could you read out the two words which is on either side of that position.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Rt. Rt is a cape, a protruding part of the coastline. So the word is Rt, R-t.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the second word? There is a second word, Gnjiliste.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Gnjiliste. I don't know how to explain that word. It's an old name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Negodic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Petrovic, sorry to keep your waiting, but I wanted to finish that little part of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that's the least of any problem. Thank you for giving me the floor. On page 25, line 3, it says: "The attack of the Yugoslav army." The witness said: "The attack of the Yugoslav navy." Could that please be corrected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreters did say navy. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Negodic, your testimony was that that position was not active on 6th of December because the position came under attack from the JNA and the crew there had to withdraw into the shelter, is it, or the hotel that was near there, the place?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said, and I said that they withdrew because fire had been opened from several ships of the Yugoslav navy, because land forces, the artillery of the Yugoslav People's Army, could not effect their position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please place your pointer on the position which is just below that position you were speaking about. If you take your pointer down. That's correct. Can you please keep your pointer there. Yes. Can you identify what that location is? And I'm asking for the location.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: The location is the area of the Neptun Hotel. I cannot give you other details. That is the reserve position of the recoilless cannon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it from your response that the weapon that was deployed there was the recoilless cannon. And you said it was a reserve position. Can you explain, please? What did you mean by reserve position?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: If we move along this map north-east of this particular position, we will notice another marking which is the same, and above it it says Rt Kantafig. That is the position of the recoilless cannon. And what you are asking me about is the reserve position which was prepared for that same recoilless cannon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I understand you, sir, when you use the word "reserve" and since we are laypersons we're not very familiar with military terms, what you mean is it's an alternative position; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you, since we're on this position, also move the map and show what its alternative position was.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: This is the alternative position, and this is the real position of the recoilless cannon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please place your pointer again on that position. No. No, the earlier -- the proper position. You're now placing your pointer on the position as I understand was the reserve position. That is correct. So this position that you're now placing your pointer on, which for the record is towards east of the word Solitudo, was the real position for this recoilless cannon?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the previous position was merely a reserve position, that is, an alternative position?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to clarify, could you explain as to how this works? When you say a reserve position, does that mean that one weapon is moved from one position to the other? Is that what you mean? According to necessity.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at --

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: As we will see later in the case of the Maljutka, when necessary, it is taken from its basic position, the recoilless cannon is, and then it is placed at its reserve position by the Hotel Neptun. It all depends on the situation or, rather, on the assessment made of the -- by the command in terms of what should be done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at a given time, that is, in one instance you will not have both positions deployed since you have only one weapon for both positions? Is that how I understand you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes. You understood me correctly. There is one artillery piece and two combat positions. One is actually a combat position, and the other one is a reserve position, as it is called.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the reserve position that you indicated near Hotel Neptun, was the recoilless cannon at the reserve position as at 6 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then was it at the combat position which is west of the word Solitudo?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It was at its basic combat position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you identify the location of that basic combat position of the recoilless cannon?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: It is the area between Solitudo and Orsan. It's a small bay, a very small bay. I don't know how else to explain it. It is the area where fishermen used to take out their boats in order to be overhauled, the old ones. This position was there just to prevent the Yugoslav navy ships from entering the port of Gruz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just going back to the reserve position. That symbol that is indicated there, is that the symbol one uses to indicate a recoilless cannon?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: That is how a recoilless cannon is indicated or marked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the symbol at the basic combat position, is it the same symbol that is indicated there?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: If you mean to the left of the basic position of the recoilless cannon, that is the combat position of the mortar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I'm referring to the basic combat position which you -- we were talking about earlier on. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That symbol, does it reflect the symbol that one uses for recoilless cannons? Because it seems quite different from the symbol which you indicated earlier on.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Perhaps it's just a mistake in the actual drawing of the map. Perhaps not enough of the red colour was used in the lower area, so it doesn't look the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you are aware by your personal knowledge that that was a position for recoilless cannon?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said, sir, that it was deployed, the recoilless cannon was deployed at this position on 6th of December, 1991. Was it active on 6th of December, 1991? Did it fire?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: I've already said what the purpose of that recoilless cannon was, to prevent the ships of the Yugoslav navy from entering the port of Gruz. Since that did not happen, there was no need to open fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that will be a convenient time for the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have a break now for some 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I proceed, I think I ought to make a correction to the record. When I referred to the recoilless cannon, the basic combat position, I referred to it as to the west of the word Solitudo. It should be the east. I got my directions wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, to the west of that recoilless cannon, just above the word Solitudo, there is a symbol. Can you first identify what that location is?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: That is the combat position of the mortar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please first identify the location. What is that location known as?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: The combat position of Solitudo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were the weapons that were positioned there? Can you give the type and the numbers?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: It was a combined unit. 120 mortars -- millimetre mortars and 82-millimetre launchers. There were three of 120 millimetres and three of 82 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the position known as the camping ground in Solitudo in Lapad?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It was an automobile camp, and that's where that particular piece was positioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That symbol, is that the type of symbol that indicates mortar positions?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, for both types.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say for both types, you mean for both calibres, the 120 and 82 millimetres?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this position deployed as at 6 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did -- did the weapons that were positioned there fire on the 6th of December, 1991, in that was the position active on the 6th?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you indicate as to which targets the weapons, the mortars positioned at this location fired at, towards which direction and at which JNA targets?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: From that position, Fort Srdj was fired at and the area around it. So Srdj was the target.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those weapons fire at Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: That assignment was one that other combat positions had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this particular position did not fire at Zarkovica on the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: No. Fort Srdj and to the north-east of Srdj which was Strincjera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on, if -- could you please move the pointer further down. And if I may have the assistance of the usher to move the map -- or perhaps Mr. Negodic can do it. Yes. Thank you. If you could just take -- move the map a little down, Mr. Negodic. Could you pull -- that's a good position, yes. Thank you. Could you move the pointer to the position indicated towards the south at the point where there is a number 10, figure 10. If you would just put your pointer there near -- just a little to the left from the mortar -- the symbol of the mortar. Further to the left. That's right. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honour, the witness is indicating right now a position south-west of the word Gospino Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, could you identify the location you're indicating right now? What is that location? And I'm referring to the location and not the weapons.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: The location is Gospino Polje, towards the sea. It could be Gorica, a settlement called Gorica today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what -- what is the -- what does that symbol indicate? What were the weapons or what was the weapon that was positioned there?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: The symbol was a single-barrel rocket launcher, and the calibre was 128 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it one such weapon or several?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: If you're talking about 1991, to the first half of December, then that is not the location of the single-barrel 128-millimetre launcher, but on this map where you can see it now at Gorica, that was a later date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know. I will come to that. I just wanted to find out when you -- that indication, does it mean one rocket launcher or several?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: No. We only had one single-barrel rocket launcher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that symbol, does it indicate rocket launchers? Is that the symbol used to indicate rocket launchers?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just -- of course you referred to it. I will ask you the question. Was this position deployed at that location on 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then could you please place your pointer and indicate as to exactly where that particular weapon was positioned on 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is that location known as?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: It is 150 metres north of the Libertas Hotel. A small hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, could you please draw a square around that rocket launcher which you indicated as not being there on the 6th of December, 1991. Just draw a square around it as clearly as possible with a blue pen.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you draw an arrow out of that square down and mark it with "A". From the square if you draw an arrow out, going towards the sea and put an "A" there.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you indicate with the same symbol the position at which this weapon was in place on the 6th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It has gone out of the -- gone out of view, but perhaps once you draw --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it has to, to be drawn. Then we'll have to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you put -- draw a circle around that position, the new position that you indicated.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And draw a square going out down to the sea and put an "A" there. Draw -- I'm sorry, not a square. Draw an arrow. Draw an arrow out of the circle and indicate it with "A".

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your testimony is that the position indicated inside the square marked "A" was in fact at the position within the circle indicated with the -- with "A" on 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on 6th of December, 1991, was the rocket launcher positioned towards the direction you drew it in? You -- your drawing is with the rocket launcher facing east. Is that the correct direction?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you indicate as to when this particular weapon was at the position within the square marked "A"?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: On the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, my question is not the circle, but when was this weapon placed at the position within the square marked "A". That is, the original position. When was it there?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: The second half of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the rocket launcher which is now indicated at the position which you said was by a hotel -- I'm sorry, I've forgotten the name. Could you replace what the location is again.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Hotel Libertas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it active on the 6th of December, 1991? Did it fire?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: In the early afternoon one rocket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that all that this particular rocket launcher fired on 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you observe that particular fire, that particular one rocket that was fired? Did you watch it? Did you observe it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: From the combat position that I was located in, the order came and you could see with the naked eye the firing at Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the rocket impact on -- I'm sorry. First my question is: Towards which direction or at which JNA target was that particular rocket fired at?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Zarkovica is an observation post and a combat position for the recoilless gun, the Maljutka, and from time to time for the cannon -- the tank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was fired at Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see the rocket impact on Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes. A truck was hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If you now move to the position where there is a weapons position just at the word Gospino Polje. Could you please place your pointer on that position, that is not east of -- that's correct, that position. Now, it is already indicated at Gospino Polje. What was the weapon that was located at this place? What does that position indicate?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: The 78-millimetre cannon Zis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many cannons were there at that position?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that position deployed as at 6 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it active on 6 December, as in did that cannon fire?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do you know towards which direction or at which JNA targets the particular weapon fired at on -- during the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes. The Srdj Fort and around the fort of Srdj and the observation post and combat position at Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, where were you on 6th of December, 1991, during the attack?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: At the combat position that I just mentioned. The cannon is underneath the bridge, and I was up on the bridge. That was the combat position and my observation post at the same time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in fact, you were present by this weapon during the course of 6 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: For most of the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this position also known as Ivo Vojnovic Road under the bridge in Lapad?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: It is underneath the bridge close to the road that is called Ivo Vojnovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please move your pointer to the mortar position that is just below that position. That is correct. What is that location? Could you please identify that location.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: It is the broader region around Gorica, between the Libertas Hotel and Gorica, moving towards the meteorological station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were the weapons or what was the weapon positioned at this location?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: There were two mortars, 120 millimetre and two 82 millimetre ones, and the combat position was set up and new weapons received in the second half of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said there were two mortars, 120 millimetre and two 82 millimetres. So is it to be taken as two mortars or three mortars? Because you said one 120 millimetres and two 82 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Two 120 ones and two 82 millimetre ones, and it was the position which was formed in the second half of November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were altogether four mortars there?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Four mortars, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this position deployed, or were those weapons in place at that location as at 6 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If not, were those weapons at another location or was that position elsewhere as at 6 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: No. We didn't have those mortars at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you get these mortars?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: In the second half of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is that position applicable for the period from the second half of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please draw a square around it? There is already a circle, but draw a square bringing this -- okay. That's all right.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you draw an arrow going out of the square and mark it with letter "B".

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please place your pointer on the position just above Gospino Polje, to the north-east of Gospino Polje where there is the word Montovjerna. That is correct. What is that location?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: That is the position of the Zis 76-millimetre cannon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does that symbol indicate the Zis 76-millimetre cannons? Is that the symbol that indicates those weapons?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes. On our map, that was the symbol denoting the 76 Zis millimetre cannon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, it is identical to the symbol just at the position marked as Gospino Polje?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the weapon or what were the weapons positioned at this location?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: The 76-millimetre Zis cannon, in the second half of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. My question -- my previous question to you was what is the location, but you identified the weapon. My first question. Could you identify what the location is by its name?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: It is the Montovjerna region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this position deployed as at 6 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: No. That position wasn't there on the 6th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you with you pointer indicate where it was positioned as at 6 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are placing your pointer at the position just about the words M. Petka. What is that location known as?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Mala Petka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, could you please draw a square around the position Montovjerna where you said was not there on 6th December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you draw an arrow going out of it towards the sea. And would you put the letter "C" there. Letter "C".

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you draw that position at the location where it was on 6 December 1991.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you put a -- draw a circle around that position.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And draw an arrow out of it and mark it "C".

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your testimony is that the position is within the square marked "C" was in fact at the position within the circle marked "C" on 6 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this position at Mala Petka, within the circle marked "C", was it active on 6 December 1991 or did fire on 6 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If so, towards which direction or at what JNA targets did it fire?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: The area of Pobrezje and Knezovi. You have Pobrezje on the map and Knezovi not on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please show where Pobrezje - I'm sorry for the pronunciation - is on the map?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the other location you indicated, towards the -- although it is not on the map, can you indicate the direction?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: It is below the Pobrezje area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is the direction towards which it fired on 6 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, four shells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Only four shells?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did that weapon fire at that particular target? Was there firing from Pobrezje or that other location you said -- mentioned on 6 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, underneath Knezovi, a recoilless gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Towards which directions was there fire from those locations, the JNA positions, where were they firing at?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: They were not able to fire because they didn't have the same range. You could just see the firing at the area of Solitudo and Gruz, which was nearer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that weapon only fired four rounds. After that what happened? Why didn't it continue firing through the day?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: The priority for the defence of Dubrovnik was given to a combined attack of artillery, infantry, and tank weapons in the area of Strincjera, Srdj, and Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, what -- what was the reason to stop after four -- after firing four rounds? Was there any reason behind -- behind the fact that you fired only four rounds and then stopped? Was this weapon used for -- at another position or was the ammunition moved?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes, you're quite right. Your assumptions are correct. The priority of the second Zis was with the targets of Srdj and Zarkovica, and it fired at those combat positions 170 shells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my question to you is: Was this weapon at Mala Petka moved or was it -- were the ammunition moved to a position that was firing? That's my question. Can you please articulate it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: The weapons remained at the combat positions. They were only transferred from that combat position -- or, rather, only ammunition was transferred to the other combat position, the one by the bridge near the street of Ivo Vojnovic

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your testimony is that it fired only four rounds and thereafter its ammunition was transferred to the position at Gospino Polje?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And therefore, that position did not have ammunition thereafter to be active with?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: A few shells were left behind only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please move your -- the pointer to the mortar position indicated to the east of the position marked Montovjerna.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. What is that location known as?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Dubrovkinja, the former barracks or simply near the SDK building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it the area of Gruz?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the area of Gruz, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were the weapons positioned at this place?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: An 82-millimetre mortar or, rather, two of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two 82-millimetre mortars?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were those weapons active on 6 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What -- towards which direction or what targets did those weapons fire at?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: The area of the Srdj Fort and around it, as well as the Zarkovica-Bosanka road towards Srdj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please move your pointer down past the Old Town to the position on the east of the Old Town, the mortar position.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is that location known as?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: It is called Lazareti, that position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were the weapons positioned there?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: Two 82-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those weapons active on 6 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC
